name: dio
_comment: H7 campaign: price BF's avoided reads.  Buffered vs direct I/O (bfdio VFS,
O_DIRECT on the main db) inside ONE campaign, shuffled, for both SUTs.
Under buffered I/O an avoided miss is usually an OS page-cache hit; under direct
I/O it is a device read, which is how ../bf-tree measures.  Every direct run is
proven by the driver's mincore residency (runner warns when the db's cached pages
grow) -- check RESULTS.md's excluded-runs table before reading any number.
Re-asks M2's split question where misses are real: ring 4/16/32 MiB of a fixed
36 MiB total, rest is pcache; stock = 36 MiB pcache (ring_bytes only pins the total).
read_zipf     point reads, scrambled zipf (hot keys spread over leaves)
read_zipfraw  point reads, contiguous zipf (hot keys share leaves)
scan_zipfraw  32-row range scans (the record cache does not serve scans)
Warmup is in OPERATIONS, not seconds, so both I/O modes start the measured phase
with the same admitted history (direct I/O runs ~3x fewer ops per second).
Report seek hit %, cached_records and evictions beside every ops/s.
